description: The third verdict. The ERC: a verifier that cannot complete a step (unreachable anchor proof, unresolvable chain) MUST report the artifact UNVERIFIABLE, distinct from both accept and reject. These cases pin that lane. Boundary deliberately encoded: a chain that CANNOT BE RESOLVED is unverifiable; a chain that resolves and finds nothing is a completed step and stays in the admit/reject lane. Run against the shipped enforcer these cases come out ADMIT or REJECT, which is the gap; the enforcer needs an unverifiable path before they reproduce.

cases.name: anchor proof unreachable, claimed pre-cutoff -> unverifiable, never classical admit
cases.comment: A pre-cutoff CLAIM with an unfetchable proof is not a proven anchor. Spec: an anchor is only a cutoff for a verifier who can fetch it. The dangerous failure is silent ADMIT on the unproven claim.

cases.name: anchor proof unreachable, post-cutoff claim with valid companion -> still unverifiable
cases.comment: The companion cannot rescue it: without the anchor time there is no in-force resolution to bind the companion to. Not a REJECT, the check never completed.

cases.name: binding chain unresolvable, post-cutoff -> unverifiable, distinct from no_in_force_binding
cases.comment: The chain source is unreachable, so in-force resolution cannot RUN. Distinct from a chain that resolves and finds no binding governing that time: that is a completed resolution and belongs to the admit/reject lane.
